beats.lead: You have heard that playing Mozart makes babies smarter
beats.text: The study behind that claim never tested a single baby.
beats.note: In 1993, researchers played Mozart's Sonata for Two Pianos to 36 college students, not infants.

beats.context: How long the spatial reasoning boost lasted, by the original researchers' own measurement.

beats.text: The study never measured IQ at all.
beats.note: It tested one narrow skill, folding paper and solving mazes. General intelligence was never on the test.

beats.name: Zell Miller
beats.role: Governor of Georgia, who proposed $105,000 a year to give every newborn a classical music CD, then played legislators Beethoven, not Mozart, and asked if they felt smarter already.

beats.lead: A 1999 study found the real cause
beats.text: People also did better after listening to a Stephen King story, if they enjoyed it.
beats.note: Researchers call it enjoyment arousal. Any music or story you like seems to work about as well as Mozart.

beats.line: It was never about the composer.
